hook.line: Running a café in La Candelaria means Tomás is up before the sun and sometimes closing after midnight. Colombians have one word for each of those, plus a tiny phrase for whose turn it is.
hook.en: I have to get up really early tomorrow.

examples.en: I have to get up really early tomorrow.
It's not good to stay up late so much.

examples.es: Vale madruga para hacer el pan.
examples.en: Vale gets up very early to make the bread.
Is it your turn to open the café tomorrow? (to a friend)
Last night I stayed up late. Today I'm tired. (a man speaking)

examples.es: A Tomás le toca cerrar el domingo.
examples.en: It's Tomás's turn to close on Sunday.

rule:
*Madrugar* means getting up very early, in the dark. It is not just "being early" (that is *llegar temprano*). *Trasnochar* is the opposite: staying up late, or missing a night's sleep.

*Me toca* + infinitive means "it's my turn" or "I'm the one who has to". The person goes in the little word: *me toca*, *te toca*, *le toca*, *nos toca*, *les toca*. The verb after it stays in the infinitive: *Me toca madrugar*.

It works like *me gusta*: the thing that happens comes after, and the person is the little word before.
smallPrint: Teachers call *tocar* here an impersonal verb of obligation, used with an indirect object, like *gustar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right word and type the whole sentence: *Mañana me toca ___.* (*madrugar* or *trasnochar*) Tomorrow I have to get up really early.
yourTurn.why: Getting up early in the dark is *madrugar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right word and type the whole sentence: *Anoche ___. Hoy estoy cansado.* (*trasnoché* or *madrugué*) Last night I stayed up late. Today I'm tired. (a man speaking)
Type in Spanish: It's Tomás's turn to open the café.
yourTurn.answer: A Tomás le toca abrir el café.
yourTurn.why: The person goes in *le*, and *a Tomás* says who.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend if it's his or her turn to close today.
yourTurn.why: *Te* is your friend, and the verb stays as *tocar* plus an infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about us: *Me toca cerrar mañana.*
yourTurn.why: Only the little word changes: *nos* for "we".

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Hoy me toca trasnochar.*
Type in Spanish: It's not good to stay up late so much.
yourTurn.why: After *es bueno*, *trasnochar* stays in the infinitive.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The person goes in the little word *me*, and the verb is *toca*.
*Madrugar* is getting up early, not arriving early. For arriving early use *llegar temprano*.
No little word goes between *toca* and the infinitive.

personal: Tell us one day when *te toca madrugar*, or a night when you *trasnochaste*.
